youtube.title: The US Government Paid Psychics to Spy for 20 Years | Project Star Gate
youtube.description:
For more than two decades, starting in the early 1970s, the CIA and later the Army and DIA funded 'remote viewing': people trying to describe distant targets with their minds. The program, run partly from Fort Meade, Maryland, went through names like Grill Flame and Sun Streak before becoming Star Gate, at a cost of about $20 million. A 1995 evaluation commissioned by the CIA found it had never produced information used to guide an intelligence operation, and recommended ending it.

📂 Case File #054: Project Star Gate

Sources: Federation of American Scientists, "STAR GATE [Controlled Remote Viewing]" https://irp.fas.org/program/collect/stargate.htm ; Wikipedia, "Stargate Project" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stargate_Project ; CIA Reading Room STARGATE collection https://www.cia.gov/readingroom/
Images: CIA floor seal (user:Duffman, public domain); SRI International HQ (Coolcaesar, CC BY-SA 3.0); Fort Meade (Ken Lund, CC BY-SA 2.0).
